tasks.description: 1.1 **[P]** Confirm SoC LLM details (API format, models, context window, limits, data retention, reachability from Vercel) and record them in the design.
1.2 **[P]** Choose values for the check input budget, per-person quotas, and maximum report range; record them in the design.
2.1 Scaffold the Next.js App Router project with TypeScript, linting, Vitest, and Playwright; commit the lockfile.
2.2 **[P]** Set up GitHub Actions: lint, type-check, unit tests, build, secret scanning, and dependency audit.
2.3 **[P]** Create the development and production Supabase projects, Vercel environments (`dev` and `master`), and GitHub OAuth apps; document every environment variable in `.env.example`.

2.4 **[P]** Create the database schema and migrations for people, projects, memberships, tasks, acceptance criteria, task events, progress updates, attached commits, check results, reports, and usage records.
3.1 Implement GitHub sign-in and sign-out with Supabase Auth, storing the verified GitHub user ID and username; add tests for first sign-in and sign-out.

3.2 Implement server-side membership and role authorization and temporary project/task API stubs for the approved routes in `identity-and-access`; add API tests for unauthenticated requests, non-members, product-manager-only actions, assigned and unassigned developer transitions, product-manager transitions, and denied requests making no state changes. Authorized stubs return HTTP 501 without mutation.

3.3 Build the public `/sign-in` page and signed-in workspace account UI with verified GitHub username and avatar, sign-out success and generic failure handling, and session-based redirects; follow `specs/ui-spec.md` and cover the identity-and-access scenarios.

4.1 **[P]** Implement project creation, keys, memberships, the one-product-manager invariant, and product-manager transfer; decide who may create a project and how its initial product manager is selected; add PostgreSQL integrity and project-route authorization tests.

4.2 **[P]** Implement task create, read, edit, reassign, and soft delete with acceptance criteria and task IDs; replace the task stubs and add API authorization tests plus tests for missing criteria, assignees outside the project, and task IDs that are never reused.

4.3 Implement the To Do → In Progress → In Review → Done lifecycle, request-changes with feedback, and progress updates; replace the state stub and add transition, assignment/permission, competing-write, and route authorization tests. Also add `version` to the task-detail read, add the read-only completion-assessment tip lookup used by submission (Developer A agreed), and replace the stub assertions in `tests/unit/project-authorization-routes.test.ts`. See "Task Lifecycle Decisions (4.3)" in `design.md`.
4.4 Build the board, task detail, and review queue pages following `specs/ui-spec.md`.

4.5 Build the create-project page and the product-manager members screen: list the project's members, add a member by GitHub username, and transfer the product-manager role, using the 4.1 routes. Add a member-listing read (left to 4.4 by D4 and deferred by B1/C4). Draft and get human approval for the spec delta and any read or route decision before implementing; add page, read-service, and authorization tests. Also add the human-approved shared "Back to Project Space" link above project tabs for both roles, pointing to `/`.

4.6 Build the product-manager New Task, edit, reassign, and delete controls on the board and task-detail pages, using the 4.2 routes and the task's current `version` (deferred by B1). Draft and get human approval for the spec delta before implementing; add rendering, role-visibility, validation, and stale-version tests.

4.7 Build the project dashboard (Header, Project Progress, Action Buttons for the product manager, Task Summary Card, Task Allocation) following `specs/ui-spec.md`, and enable its navigation tab (deferred by B1/B4). Draft and get human approval for the spec delta and its read service before implementing; add read-service and rendering tests.

5.1 **[P]** Implement the product-manager repository authorization/link flow: start a server-side setup attempt bound to the project and verified PM with single-use state and a 10-minute expiry; verify the GitHub installation through separate user authorization before listing repositories; retain a normalized server-side repository-list snapshot with a 10-minute expiry and no OAuth-token persistence; and link only a repository from that verified snapshot after rechecking current App access. Any failure leaves an existing binding unchanged. Implement the approved setup callback, snapshot-read, and final-link route contracts in `specs/github-evidence/spec.md`. Add product-manager authorization, failed-link, and PostgreSQL integrity tests. Add OAuth client ID/secret settings to server config and `.env.example`, plus minimal composition wiring. Task 5.3 provides the setup URL entry point and UI. Create a new versioned migration to replace the shipped PAT ciphertext columns with installation and repository IDs and add normalized attempt/snapshot storage; do not edit the shipped migration. Clear any legacy repository fields and PAT ciphertext so affected projects become unlinked for PM relinking. Developer A owns all Section 5 work and migrations by explicit human-approved exception to the general migration ownership rule in `AGENTS.md`. PostgreSQL migration/integrity tests were completed in the remote development environment, as confirmed by the user on 2026-11-06.

5.2 **[P]** Implement the server-side GitHub App adapter and deterministic fake. Use GitHub REST API version `2026-03-10`; mint short-lived installation tokens restricted to one linked repository with read-only permissions; list branches and commits by verified author, date range, and branch; fetch diffs; and test safe provider-error handling and token scoping.

5.3 Wire the remaining App environment configuration and repository-read adapter composition; provide the PM-only setup URL route; build the PM Project Settings repository panel and developer commit picker; and implement the approved task-scoped branch/commit listing and idempotent commit attachment routes. Add only the minimal task-detail host page needed to open and mount the commit picker because the task-detail page from 4.4 does not yet exist. Update `.env.example`. Add assigned-developer route authorization tests and tests for branch choices, date filters, task-ID preselection, no commits found, unavailable evidence, foreign authors, atomic refusal, and already-attached SHA idempotency.
6.1 **[P]** Implement the SoC LLM adapter and a deterministic fake adapter.
6.2 **[P]** Implement secret redaction; add unit tests for common secret patterns.

6.3 Implement the gateway: prompt building with untrusted content separated, schema validation with one retry, safe errors, per-person rate limits and quotas (reserved before the call, reset at 00:00 SGT, cached results not counted), and usage records; add unit tests for each.

7.1 Implement diff filtering, repository-owned `.acceptance-check.json` loading from the current default-branch tip, normalization and hashing of category prefixes, exact lockfile basenames, and generated path prefixes, GitHub-marked binary exclusion, destination-path handling for renames, and the 48,000-character budget; add tests for exclusions, priority ordering, whole-file selection, skipped-file reporting, and safe refusal when configuration is missing, invalid, or unavailable.

7.2 Implement the check service: per-criterion result, evidence verification against the diff, and caching by task, commit-set hash, criteria hash, and normalized path-rules hash; add fake-adapter tests for success, failure, unverifiable evidence, and cache hits. Add a new versioned migration and PostgreSQL integration tests for `check_results.path_rules_hash` and the corresponding uniqueness keys. Developer B owns the database migration and persistence tests; Developer A owns the check service. Do not modify shipped migrations.

7.3 Add the task-scoped assigned-developer check API, Acceptance Criteria Check UI/history component, and the read-only task-detail GET DTO that exposes check history; add assigned-developer and product-manager task-detail result-access API tests, plus tests that a check never changes task state. The read-only GET slice is a Group 7 exception to Task 4.2 ownership; Task 4.2 retains task create/edit/reassign/delete and other task writes. Task 4.3 retains lifecycle and submission state changes, and Task 4.4 retains task-detail and review-queue page integration. Group 7 does not implement a review-queue API/page, submission, or task-state changes.

8.1 Implement report input assembly from structured activity for a date range in SGT; add tests for range boundaries (including late-evening activity), excluded diffs, empty ranges, ranges longer than 7 days, and activity over the input budget.
8.2 Implement report generation with citation checks and caching invalidated by new activity; add fake-adapter tests and product-manager-only API authorization tests.
8.3 Build the report page and the project AI usage view; add product-manager-only project usage API authorization tests.

9.1 **[P]** Run the AI security evaluation: prompt-injection and secret-redaction fixtures for both AI features against the live SoC LLM in development; record outcomes without asserting exact model wording.
9.2 **[P]** Write end-to-end tests for one complete developer journey and one complete product-manager journey, including fake-provider success and failure paths.
9.3 **[P]** Run accessibility checks on the main pages and record results.

9.4 Deploy to production, run the release checks (including one real SoC LLM call from each environment, after confirming with `GET /v1/models` that each key can use the pinned model, and a GitHub sign-in on each environment that returns to that environment's own URL), and record commands, revision, environment, results, and evidence paths.
9.5 Run OpenSpec validation and all lint, type-check, test, and build checks; resolve findings and record the final results.

Pause if you hit blockers or need clarification.
